sections.label: MAS Amendment Bill 2017 powers
sections.summary: The MAS (Amendment) Bill 2017 introduces additional powers and tools to enhance Singapore's resolution regime and align it with international developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today's MAS (Amendment) Bill 2017 introduces additional powers and tools to enhance Singapore's resolution regime and bring it up to date with these international developments.

sections.label: Statutory bail-in regime
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a statutory bail-in regime letting MAS write down or convert an FI's debt into equity, applied to locally-incorporated banks and bank holding companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a statutory bail-in regime to enable MAS to write down or convert an FI's debt into equity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For now, the bail-in tool will be applied to locally-incorporated banks and bank holding companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The scope of bail-in will be limited to unsecured subordinated debt and loans, contingent convertible instruments and other existing instruments that already have bail-in clauses.

sections.label: Resolution Funding Arrangements
sections.summary: The Bill proposes Resolution Funding Arrangements to support the implementation of resolution measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, proposes to put in place Resolution Funding Arrangements to support the implementation of resolution measures.

sections.label: Reserves and supervisory objective
sections.summary: The Resolution Funding Arrangements have no implications on Singapore's reserves as funds are fully recovered from the industry, and MAS' development objective is subordinate to its supervisory objective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The proposed Resolution Funding Arrangements do not have any implications on Singapore's reserves, since the funds used will be fully recovered from the industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new provision that explicitly states that when carrying out its functions and duties, MAS' development objective of growing Singapore into an internationally competitive financial centre is subordinate to its supervisory objective of fostering financial stability.

sections.label: MAS returning profits to Government
sections.summary: Under the amended Act, MAS can return profits to the Government so long as its general reserve fund is positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under the amended Act, MAS will be able to return profits to the Government so long as its general reserve fund is positive.

sections.label: Delegation and operational updates
sections.summary: The amendments allow the Managing Director to delegate certain seal-related powers to a Deputy Managing Director, and introduce updates to MAS' mission statement and operational efficiencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The amendments will also allow the Managing Director to delegate his power – in relation to signing documents which require the MAS common seal and witnessing the affixing of the seal – to an MAS officer who holds the appointment of Deputy Managing Director or its equivalent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Such documents include powers of attorney and those relating to the issuance of sukuks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill also introduces other timely updates to MAS' mission statement and amendments to achieve greater operational efficiencies within MAS.

sections.label: Recovery and Resolution Planning welcomed
sections.summary: The passage welcomes requiring pertinent financial institutions to have Recovery and Resolution Planning, strengthening the region's financial hub standing.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will also strengthen our standing as a strong financial hub in this region.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome the move to require pertinent FIs to have in place Recovery and Resolution Planning (RRP).

sections.label: Overseas firms cheating Singaporeans
sections.summary: Malaysian firm JJPTR recruited Singaporean investors despite MAS' Alert List, and many dodgy firms cheated Singaporeans out of hundreds of millions.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, Malaysian financial firm JJPTR that had left many investors high and dry, was actively recruiting Singaporean investors through a local chatline and bank account.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Despite MAS' Alert List, many dodgy firms have managed to cheat Singaporeans out of hundreds of millions of dollars.

sections.label: Overseas companies and investor protection
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Bill protects investors when companies are based overseas, and welcomes subordinating MAS' developmental objectives to supervision objectives.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If these companies are based overseas, how can the Bill protect the investors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In particular, the new provision that subordinates MAS' developmental objectives to its supervision objectives, a recommendation emerging from the 2013 IMF financial sector assessment programme, is welcome.

sections.label: Creditors' rights and depositors
sections.summary: Part of the Bill relates to creditors and their rights, but it is unclear whether depositors and policyholders are included.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Part of the Bill relates to creditors and their rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But it is not entirely clear to me if depositors and policyholders are included in this category.

sections.label: RRP requirements for banks
sections.summary: New RRP requirements apply to domestic systemically important banks and other banks assessed to have systemic impact or maintain critical functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new RRP requirements, for example, apply to domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs) as well as "other banks that are assessed to have systemic impact or that maintain critical functions".

sections.label: Banks' IT systems and BCBS 239
sections.summary: The passage asks whether banks' expectation to maintain IT systems producing timely data is met by complying with BCBS 239.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is the expectation for banks to maintain IT systems which can produce data in a timely manner basically met if a bank complies with the Basel Committee's Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239)?

sections.label: 2009 record lay-offs
sections.summary: Singapore saw a record 23,430 lay-offs in 2009 due to the Global Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2009, Singapore saw a record number of lay-offs − 23,430 to be exact − due to the effects of the Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: 2016 financial sector redundancies
sections.summary: In 2016, the financial and insurance services sector saw 2,310 redundancies, 2,090 of them PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2016, the financial and insurance services sector saw 2,310 redundancies with 2,090 being Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMETs).

sections.label: Financial Sector Tripartite Committee
sections.summary: The Financial Sector Tripartite Committee was set up last year to bring tripartite partners together for a financial workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Financial Sector Tripartite Committee was set up last year to bring together the tripartite partners to foster a financial workforce that can meet the changing needs and demands of the financial industry through the implementation of various initiatives and programmes.

sections.label: Preparing for financial upheavals
sections.summary: Singapore has not had a bank failure, but strengthened efforts and the enhanced framework will better prepare it for financial upheavals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: While Singapore has not had a bank failure, no one can guarantee that such a situation would never arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To sum up, I believe that strengthened efforts in these two areas, coupled with the implementation of the enhanced framework in the proposed Bill, will better prepare Singapore for any upheavals in our financial system.

sections.label: Recovery plans for FIs
sections.summary: The Bill requires FIs to prepare and maintain recovery plans and submit them to MAS for resolution planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill before the House requires FIs to prepare and maintain recovery plans and submit them to MAS for resolution planning.

sections.label: MAS notice to FIs
sections.summary: The Bill allows MAS to issue a notice to a pertinent FI to prepare a plan to restore its financial strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill allows MAS to issue a notice to a pertinent FI to prepare, in the form and manner and containing the information specified in the notice, a plan to restore the financial strength and viability of the FI in the event it suffers financial pressure.

sections.label: Penalties for contravening FI order
sections.summary: An FI contravening an order under subsection (1) faces a fine up to $250,000 on conviction, plus up to $25,000 per day for continuing offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: An FI that contravenes an order under subsection (1) is subject, upon conviction, to a fine not exceeding $250,000 and, in the case of a continuing offence, to a further fine not exceeding $25,000 for every day or part of a day during which the offence continues after conviction.

sections.label: DI Fund supporting resolution measure
sections.summary: Under clause 39's amendments, the Deposit Insurance Fund may support a resolution measure under the MAS Act taken on a DI Scheme member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the case of the Deposit Insurance and Policy Owners' Protection Schemes Act amendments in clause 39, the Deposit Insurance Fund or DI Fund may be used to support a resolution measure under the MAS Act that is taken on a DI Scheme member.

sections.label: MAS public education after Bill
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MAS will conduct public education so everyone, especially the man-in-the-street, understands in simplified language how depositors and policyholders are protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: After the passage of this Bill, I also hope MAS would do a public education exercise so that everyone, especially the man-in-the-street, can understand in simplified language how our Government is taking steps to protect FI depositors and insurance policyholders as we strengthen our financial framework.

sections.label: Recovery and resolution planning powers
sections.summary: Clause 12 gives MAS powers to direct FIs facing financial pressure to produce a recovery plan and take measures for orderly resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Turning to clause 12 which, if I can interpret it well, is Recovery and Resolution Planning for FIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This clause gives MAS powers to direct FIs that are facing financial pressure to come up with a recovery plan and direct that institution to take certain measures for its orderly resolution.

sections.label: MAS bail-in of FI instruments
sections.summary: The amendment empowers MAS to bail-in instruments of ownership and liabilities of the affected FI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment to the Bill will empower MAS to bail-in instruments of ownership and liabilities of the affected FI.

sections.label: Bail-in amendments welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes amendments giving MAS the call to bail-in institutions, affording shareholders and creditors greater protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The impact of a totally free and open market, when it turns south, is, indeed, a national worry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, the amendments which provide MAS the call to bail-in these institutions, affording shareholders and creditors a greater amount of protection, are welcomed.

sections.label: Pros outweigh cons, Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker believes the pros outweigh the cons and supports the change to the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While it may, I believe the pros outweigh the cons − a positive change to the Bill which I support.

sections.label: Support for Recovery and Resolution Planning
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill adopting Recovery and Resolution Planning, already in the US, EU, Japan and Hong Kong, and MAS powers over recovery plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, I stand in support of the Bill, which ushers in the adoption of Recovery and Resolution Planning which is already in place in the US, the EU, as well as in Japan and Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support the ability of MAS to require a recovery plan from pertinent FIs and to instruct implementation of the recovery plan.

sections.label: Support for bail-in regime
sections.summary: The speaker supports a bail-in regime where a distressed FI is rescued not by taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I support as well the introduction of a bail-in regime where a distressed FI is rescued not by the taxpayers.

sections.label: Government and Board agreement required
sections.summary: The change requires both the Government and the Board to agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, it results in requiring both the Government and the Board to agree.

sections.label: Government unilateral approval replaced
sections.summary: The Government's ability to approve and decide unilaterally is replaced by the need to agree with the Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, why is the Government's ability to approve and decide unilaterally replaced with the need for the Government to agree with the Board?

sections.label: D-SIBs have recovery plans
sections.summary: All domestic systemically important banks already have recovery plans submitted and in place, and they are the banks subject to RRPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In fact, all our domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs) already have recovery plans submitted and in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In response to Mr Leon Perera on which are the banks that are subjected to RRPs, in fact, they are currently the D-SIBs.

sections.label: Phased RRP requirements for FIs
sections.summary: RRP requirements will be phased in proportionately, based on FIs' systemic importance to the financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: RRP requirements will be phased in and applied in a proportionate manner, based on the FIs' systemic importance to the financial system.

sections.label: Penalties at highest supervisory level
sections.summary: The penalties pegged now are already at the highest level in the supervisory framework for licensing breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The penalties pegged now are actually already to the highest level of penalties in our supervisory framework for licensing breaches.

sections.label: Depositors and policy owners not covered
sections.summary: Depositors and policy owners are not covered under the bail-in scope, which is restricted to unsecured subordinated debt and loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera asked if depositors and policy owners are protected under the creditor compensation framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They are not covered under the scope of bail-in of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The bail-in regime that I have described in the Second Reading speech will be restricted to unsecured subordinated debt, as well as loans.

sections.label: MAS initial loan to Resolution Fund
sections.summary: MAS will provide the initial liquidity loan to the Resolution Fund, recovered from the industry via ex-post levies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS will provide the initial liquidity loan to the Resolution Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The loan will eventually be recovered from the industry via ex-post levies.

sections.label: Trustee duties and record-keeping
sections.summary: The appointed trustee must have capacity, experience and expertise, and MAS intends to require proper accounts and records after the Resolution Fund's dissolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The appointed trustee must have the capacity, experience and expertise to carry out its duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To ensure the integrity and the accountability of the resolution funding process, MAS intends to require the trustee to keep proper accounts and records of transactions for a period after the dissolution of the Resolution Fund.

sections.label: Protecting policy owners of non-viable insurers
sections.summary: For a non-viable insurer, MAS prioritises policy owner protection, and the Policy Owners' Protection Funds or Resolution Fund can be tapped for coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Should an insurer become non-viable, apart from securing financial stability, MAS will also prioritise the protection of policy owners, including through ensuring continuity in their insurance coverage and, where possible, limiting the financial loss that they could suffer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To this end, the Policy Owners' Protection Funds or the Resolution Fund can be tapped on so that policy owners can retain their insurance coverage.

sections.label: MAS capital approval governance
sections.summary: The Bill requires both the MAS Board and the Government to agree on revisions to MAS' paid-up capital, and updates MAS' mission and objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Requiring the agreement of both the MAS Board and the Government strengthens the governance of these decisions and ensures the financial implications on both parties are adequately taken into account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In approving any revisions to its paid-up capital, the MAS Board must make sure that MAS' capital and reserves remain adequate for it to carry out its principal objects and functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Government is the sole owner of MAS' paid-up capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Bill also introduces updates to clarify MAS' mission and objectives as well as other timely amendments to achieve greater operational efficiencies within MAS.
